title: PyTorch Introduction — Put Layers Inside a Module
key_insight: A class derived from `nn.Module` registers its layers and parameters. Its `forward` method describes how an input travels through them.
body:
## Put Layers Inside a Module

A model has several layers and learned weights that must be saved, moved, and called together. Loose variables become hard to manage.

A class derived from `nn.Module` registers its layers and parameters. Its `forward` method describes how an input travels through them.

Calling the model runs that forward route. The module can then switch modes, move devices, and expose all trainable parameters to an optimizer.
common_mistakes: A tensor can contain only one number.
An nn.Module prevents parameters from being trained.
Autograd requires every derivative to be entered by hand.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Put Layers Inside a Module” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: PyTorch turns the phase’s equations into inspectable, trainable programs.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Put Layers Inside a Module” situation, explain PyTorch Introduction without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
